title: Weather and zero-shot forecasting models: backtest results for GB electricity demand (part 1 of 2)
claim: In a preregistered 960-day day-ahead backtest on GB national demand, identical honestly timed weather forecasts cut error for Chronos-2, Timestral-209M, TimesFM 2.5 and a weekly-lag regression, and the models' lead over the regression mostly vanishes once the regression has weather.
why_relevant: The design our benchmark mirrors: zero-shot foundation models against a lag regression on the same forecast-regime weather, on national load a day ahead rather than zonal load a week ahead.

title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Load Forecasting Under Covariate Uncertainty
claim: On three load datasets Chronos-2 is the most accurate zero-shot and fine-tuned when future covariates are known or well forecast, but it degrades as covariate forecasts get noisier, where TimesNet holds up better.
why_relevant: Tests the oracle-versus-forecast covariate gap for foundation models on electric load, which is what our two weather regimes separate.

title: PJM Cold-Spell Calibration Benchmark: When Cold-Spell Calibration Fails to Transfer
claim: In a pre-registered benchmark over four PJM extreme-cold events, 90% load-forecast intervals lose coverage inside the events and no conformal calibrator chosen without the target event restores it; leave-one-event-out evaluation overstates coverage against chronological evaluation.
why_relevant: PJM load with temperature under a frozen protocol; day-ahead and probabilistic rather than week-ahead point forecasts, and no foundation models.

title: Assessing Covariate-Informed Grid Load Forecasting with a Time-Series Foundation Model
claim: On ISO New England and ENTSO-E load, Chronos-2 with covariates gains substantially from task-specific fine-tuning and is strong at short horizons against task-specific deep learning models.
why_relevant: Chronos-2 with exogenous inputs on US ISO load is the model and setting of our primary comparison.

title: EnergyBench: a live, gate-aligned benchmark of day-ahead forecasts for European power markets
claim: A live daily benchmark that runs eighteen foundation models, linear and boosted models and operator forecasts on one frozen information set for six European zones; over the first 32 live days weather covariates lowered the error of every foundation model run with and without them.
why_relevant: Same-inputs comparison of foundation models with and without forecast weather on zonal load, live rather than backtested and day-ahead.

title: Timestral
claim: Mistral's four open-weight forecasting models (5M to 209M parameters) are reported to lead GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench among zero-shot models and accept known-future covariates.
why_relevant: Timestral-209M is already a runnable model in the spec that takes temperature; this is its primary source.

title: TimesFM 3.0
claim: Google's 330M-parameter TimesFM 3.0 forecasts multivariate series zero-shot with past and known-future covariates and is reported top among pretrained models on GIFT-Eval, fev-bench and TIME; the weights carry a non-commercial licence.
why_relevant: A covariate-capable successor to the TimesFM 2.5 row on our leaderboard, listed in the spec as running with temperature through FoundationForecast.

title: t0: A Time-Series Foundation Model for Forecasting with Context
claim: The open-weight t0 models condition on past and known-future covariates without retraining; known-future covariates raise t0-alpha's skill by about six points over 30 tasks, and the later t0-gamma card reports gains over t0-beta on every listed benchmark.
why_relevant: A covariate-aware zero-shot model with Apache-2.0 weights that the spec lists as able to take temperature.

title: How Far Does Zero-Shot Go? A Leakage-Aware Evaluation of TimesFM 3 on Post-Release, Multivariate and Controlled Data
claim: Under a protocol frozen before the test data existed, TimesFM 3 beats a pre-specified classical ensemble on post-release data including electricity load, but in two prospective weeks its point-forecast lead on load is not confirmed and its 80% intervals cover about 70%.
why_relevant: Post-release evaluation of a foundation model on electricity load answers the training-overlap question our weights rule is about.

title: A Benchmark for Electrical Load Forecasting Across Grid Levels: Time-Series Transformers Outperform Established Methods
claim: Across a control area, low-voltage feeders and end consumers, Transformer forecasters cut short-term load error by roughly 7 to 11% against established methods, and zero-shot Chronos-2 is competitive on two datasets but misses special events on the control-area data.
why_relevant: Includes control-area load with covariates and a zero-shot Chronos-2 row, at short horizons.

title: Combining Weather Forecast Aggregation and State-Space Models for Adaptive Probabilistic Electricity Load Forecasting
claim: For French national load, an adaptive additive model fed several weather-forecast providers at once beats single-provider versions, most clearly for probabilistic forecasts and extreme quantiles.
why_relevant: About how weather-forecast error enters a load forecast, which is our forecast regime; a statistical model rather than a foundation model.

title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Time Series Foundation Models for Electrical Load Forecasting
claim: Across four load aggregation levels pretrained Moirai and Chronos-2 beat seasonal naive and XGBoost baselines, and rank-16 LoRA on Moirai Large cuts normalised MAE by about 7.5% while updating about 1% of the weights.
why_relevant: Electric load with Chronos-2 against a boosted-tree baseline; about fine-tuning, which our zero-shot rows do not use.

title: Peak-Aware Short-Term Load Forecasting Across Distribution Grid Aggregation Levels
claim: On UK and Swiss distribution data Chronos-2 has the lowest high-demand-period error at every aggregation level, 20 to 51% below LightGBM and XGBoost.
why_relevant: Chronos-2 against LightGBM on load, with peak hours scored separately; distribution level and short horizon.

title: pl-forecast-bench: a leakage-checked forecasting benchmark for the Polish power system
claim: A benchmark that fixes data, as-of rules for every input, a 12-month test year and reference models (naive, operator plan, ridge, boosting, zero-shot foundation models) for Polish demand, wind, solar and price, with tests that detect look-ahead.
why_relevant: National demand with archived weather forecasts and explicit no-lookahead rules, the discipline our harness enforces; day-ahead and intraday.

title: Systematic Evaluation of TabPFN-TS and Chronos-2 for Zero-Shot Heat Load Forecasting in District Heating Networks
claim: For hourly 24-hour heat-load forecasts in two German networks, zero-shot TabPFN-TS and Chronos-2 with ambient temperature beat every trained baseline on point accuracy over a full year; the main benchmark assumes perfect weather, with a separate forecast-weather sensitivity run.
why_relevant: Temperature-driven hourly energy series with an oracle run and a forecast-weather run, heat rather than electric load.

title: Machine Learning and Time-Series Foundation Models for Day-Ahead Electricity Forecasting in a University Building
claim: On 57 test days for one building TimesFM 3.0 with covariates has the lowest error, about 43% below weekly seasonal naive, but paired comparisons do not separate it from XGBoost, and covariates help only on holidays.
why_relevant: TimesFM 3.0 with weather covariates on hourly electricity; one building, observed weather and a test window under 90 days.

title: Zero-shot time-series foundation models against the Khepri v1.5 baselines for 96-hour carbon-intensity forecasts in nine Nordic bidding zones: a preregistered comparison
claim: In a preregistered comparison, univariate Timestral and Chronos-2 have lower MAPE than SARIMA and boosted baselines for 96-hour carbon-intensity forecasts on a 2025 test year, while a 14-origin post-release holdout is within the minimum detectable effect and reported as undetermined.
why_relevant: A preregistered multi-day zonal backtest of two models we run, with a post-release holdout; the target is carbon intensity and no covariates are used.

title: The Hidden Look-Ahead: Point-in-Time Leakage in Electricity Market Data
claim: Choosing the latest weather-model run issued before an auction gate picks a run that was not yet published on over 99% of days for six of ten configurations in Great Britain, with an apparent accuracy effect between -9% and +24%.
why_relevant: Bears on how our forecast regime selects lead-matched archived forecasts without lookahead; it is a data-timing study, not a forecasting method.

title: On the Encoding of Calendar Features in Covariate-Informed Time Series Foundation Models
claim: Across four covariate-aware foundation models and nine calendar-driven datasets, the choice among seven calendar encodings changes zero-shot MASE by up to about 10% on ordinary days and far more on holidays.
why_relevant: A way to change what covariate-aware models such as Chronos-2 get from holiday inputs, which our regression baseline already uses.

title: Multi-horizon forecasting of national electricity demand in Türkiye: run records, forecasts and trained models
claim: An archive of 759 training runs with sealed test forecasts for national demand at several horizons using calendar, holiday and temperature inputs; the record itself states no headline number.
why_relevant: National load with temperature and holidays across horizons with a sealed test set; trained models rather than zero-shot.

title: Closed-Form Calendar Estimation in Deep Load Forecasting: An Information-Controlled Benchmark on Eight National Grids
claim: Companion archive of per-window errors and probabilistic runs for a benchmark of deep load forecasters on eight national grids that controls what calendar information each model gets; the record states no headline number.
why_relevant: National load forecasting where every model is held to the same information, the same rule as our same-inputs requirement.

title: TimeH2O-v1
claim: H2O.ai's 108M-parameter model takes a target with optional covariates and its card reports leading zero-shot scores on GIFT-Eval and fev-bench; weights are gated under a non-commercial licence, with paper and code not yet out.
why_relevant: The spec lists TimeH2O as able to take temperature through FoundationForecast.

title: Timer-M1: A Multivariate Time Series Foundation Model via Learning Primitives
claim: A pretrained multivariate model trained on synthesised episodes with target, past-only and known-future covariate roles is reported first on fev-bench and TIME and second on GIFT-Eval.
why_relevant: A new zero-shot model with known-future covariates; whether weights are public is not stated in the abstract.

title: Forecasting Associations, Not Interventions: A Preregistered Causal Audit of Covariate-Aware Time Series Foundation Models
claim: On a preregistered grid with exact counterfactuals, Chronos-2, TiRex-2, TabPFN-TS and TimesFM 2.5 respond to a future covariate path associationally and more confounded than a regression does.
why_relevant: Describes how the covariate-aware models we run use a future temperature path compared with a regression.

title: A Later Test Set Is Not a New Domain: Pretraining Familiarity Survives a Contamination-Free Hold-Out
claim: On data published after every tested model was released, pretrained forecasters win five of seven groups, and their advantage tracks how familiar the domain is from pretraining rather than seasonality.
why_relevant: Relevant to reading our rows whose scored weeks fall after the weights date; not specific to load.

title: Foundation or Formula? A Simulation-Based Comparison of Google's TimesFM-3 and Classical Time-Series Models
claim: On 7,200 simulated series under a pre-registered protocol neither TimesFM-3 nor classical methods dominate: TimesFM-3 is never far from the best method, while automatic ARIMA is 21 to 24% better on seasonal data with four or more cycles.
why_relevant: A pre-registered foundation-model-versus-classical comparison free of training overlap; synthetic univariate data at a 12-step horizon.

title: Tabby: An Open Pretraining Recipe for Time Series Foundation Models
claim: A 145M-parameter open model with contexts up to 8,192 points and a published training recipe is reported competitive zero-shot on GIFT-Eval and TIME.
why_relevant: Listed in the spec as a FoundationForecast wrapper that runs on load history only.

title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
claim: A flow-matching model that generates whole future paths, distilled to one or two steps, is reported competitive on fev-bench and TIME and best on a new path-score benchmark that scores peak load and cumulative demand.
why_relevant: An open-weight model aimed at path quantities such as weekly peak; not load-specific and covariate use is not stated.

title: Medium-Term Multi-Resolution Electric Load Forecasting using Economic Data and Foundation Model
claim: For French load forecast 1 to 48 months ahead with a tabular foundation model, selected economic covariates improve skill by about 20% over 2015 to 2025.
why_relevant: Electric load with a foundation model and covariates, at monthly-to-yearly horizons far beyond a week.

title: U.S. utility load forecasts filed on FERC Form 714, 2006-2025: forecast errors, weather-normalized outcomes, prediction intervals and capacity decision rules
claim: Code and data scoring about 13,700 filed peak and energy forecasts from US balancing authorities, PJM's own included, against weather-normalised outcomes, with intervals built from past errors.
why_relevant: US load forecasts including PJM, but seasonal and annual planning forecasts rather than hourly week-ahead.

title: PatchTST-FM-r2 (IBM Granite)
claim: IBM's 385M-parameter zero-shot model is described on its card as the top GIFT-Eval model under a permissive commercial-friendly licence.
why_relevant: Listed in the spec as a univariate FoundationForecast wrapper; Apache-2.0 weights.

title: Tafsut Univariate Base
claim: A 105M-parameter MIT-licensed univariate model whose card places it third on CRPS and fourth on MASE among twelve models on GIFT-Eval.
why_relevant: Listed in the spec as a univariate FoundationForecast wrapper; it takes no covariates.

title: gridload-compact
claim: Two small quantile networks (about 160k parameters) trained on German net-load history are self-scored on the TS-Arena archive as ahead of the best reference model at 24 hours and tied with Chronos-2 at 72 hours; the card says its own pre-registered live go/no-go rule failed.
why_relevant: A load specialist compared with zero-shot foundation models up to three days ahead, with calendar inputs and no weather.

title: Thaki EnergyLoad Forecaster v0.1
claim: Three LightGBM models for per-meter load at 15 minutes, 1 hour and 24 hours on the public UCI Portuguese dataset beat persistence and seasonal naive on MASE on a 2014 test half-year.
why_relevant: A LightGBM load baseline with lag and calendar features; meter-level, no weather and at most a day ahead.

title: A controlled benchmark of temporal dependence for day-ahead electricity-demand discrepancies in Great Britain
claim: A retrospective benchmark on 364 days of 2024 comparing independent, Gaussian-copula and empirical ensembles of day-ahead demand forecast discrepancies, keeping adverse and inconclusive findings.
why_relevant: About the error structure of national day-ahead load forecasts rather than a forecasting method.

title: Türkiye Grid Foundation Model
claim: Research software for studying transfer across electricity consumption, renewable generation and day-ahead price in Türkiye with chronological evaluation; the record states no result.
why_relevant: A grid-specific pretrained forecaster that covers consumption; no stated accuracy and no weather inputs mentioned.

title: Zero-shot time series foundation models for statistical postprocessing of weather forecasts: how much training data do they replace?
claim: Code release for a comparison of zero-shot TimesFM-3 and Chronos-2, given the ensemble mean as a covariate, with trained statistical postprocessing of 2 m temperature forecasts at 49 German stations.
why_relevant: Uses a weather forecast as a known-future covariate for zero-shot models; the target is temperature, not load.

title: BQEB ForecastBench: Benchmarking AI Models for Smart Grid Forecasting Using BQEB-Data v1
claim: An open benchmark for next-hour load and day-ahead price forecasting that scores linear regression, random forest and gradient boosting under one chronological split.
why_relevant: A load benchmark with classical baselines only, at a one-hour horizon.

title: sktime v1.2.0
claim: The sktime 1.2.0 release adds forecaster wrappers for Tafsut, TimesFM 3, TiRex-2 and t0.
why_relevant: A second route, beside FoundationForecast, to run the new covariate-capable models from one interface.

title: sktime v1.0.2
claim: The sktime 1.0.2 release adds Moirai 2.0, Sundial and WindFM forecasters.
why_relevant: Library support for pretrained forecasters; none of the added models takes temperature in our setup.
